queryResult.TName: BATTERY: Drains Too Fast/Not Holding Charge
queryResult.htmlBody:
Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




The published up-to playtime is the maximum battery time you will get when listening at background levels. As you turn up the volume, the playtime will be reduced, much like a phone battery when you brighten the screen. The same goes for source material. Music with more bass will also reduce playtime. It is possible that the battery is working correctly, but depletes more quickly when the volume is very loud and/or the bass has been boosted.




Please try this experiment:




Charge the battery to 100% and then listen to music without any bass boosted, and at a very low volume. If the battery lasts close to the published up-to playtime, the battery is working fine. However, if you get less than 90% of the published spec, this likely means that the battery is losing its capacity.




Note: Battery playtime also decreases as the battery ages.




Should you determine that the battery is losing its capacity...

Note: For your reference, your case number is {!Case.CaseNumber}.




Regards,

There are 4 potential causes for a problem like this.
  • Bad Charging cable
  • Bad Power adapter
  • Charging Port Issue
  • Battery Issue

Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




There are 4 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Another source device (Phone, Tablet, Computer, etc.) is connected to the product

  • Recent App or Operating System Update

  • New or additional nearby wireless activity

  • Source device issue


Please try the following steps in order to determine the problem.





If the Bluetooth indicator is solid:




    This means another source device is connected to the product. Locate the source device that is connected and turn off Bluetooth. This will enable your source device to reconnect to the product. If your device does not automatically reconnect, go to the device's Bluetooth settings to manually connect it to the product.




    If this did not solve the problem, please continue to “Additional Steps”.







If the Bluetooth indicator is blinking:




    This means that the product is in pairing mode, but not connected to anything.






    • If your Bluetooth on the source device is not On, go to your Bluetooth settings and turn it on. It should automatically reconnect.

    • If it doesn't automatically reconnect, manually connect the source device to the product by selecting the product from your Bluetooth list.




    If this did not solve the problem, please continue to “Additional Steps”.






If the Bluetooth indicator is off:




    Typically, the product will automatically reconnect to the last source device it was connected to. If that device is not nearby or if its Bluetooth is currently turned off, the product will not automatically reconnect.






    • Turn on Bluetooth on your source device, it should automatically reconnect to the product

    • If it does not automatically reconnect, go to your device's Bluetooth settings to manually connect the device to the product.




    If this did not solve the problem, please continue to “Additional Steps”.






Additional Steps



  1. Refresh Pairing



      Sometimes, new or additional wireless activity near you may cause a break in pairing. Additionally, operating system or app updates can break the pairing between the source device and the product. Refresh the pairing between the source device and the product.






      1. Turn product off

      2. Forget/Unpair the product name from the source device

      3. Reboot your source device

      4. Turn product on

      5. Perform pairing

    To reset,
    [List Steps Here]




    After the reset is complete, repeat the pairing process outlined in Step 1, “Refresh Pairing”, to pair the product with your source device again.




If this does not solve the problem, please continue to “Next Steps”.

Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




There are 3 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Volume Level

  • EQ Settings

  • Source Device



Note: Buzzing, popping, and static are all referred to as distortion.






If the issue is affected as the volume changes






Source devices (phones, tablets, etc.) all behave a bit differently. Some have very loud outputs, and some can be quite a bit lower, even at maximum volumes. The same goes for individual songs, some are louder than others. It is possible that the output level of your source device or song causes the unit to reach maximum undistorted volume before actually reaching 100% on the volume control. So, if the issue only occurs when the volume is getting near to maximum, this would confirm that the issue is the result of an extremely loud source device or song recording.




On the other hand, if you are using an Equalizer (EQ) to boost frequencies, this has the same effect as increasing the volume. Try turning the EQ off. If the sound no longer distorts with the EQ off, the speaker is not damaged and the EQ settings need to be adjusted to prevent distortion and eventual damage.




However, if the issue continues, try to connect a different device to the headphones to determine if the problem is with the device or headphones.




*If the headphones model can’t be reset, please remove this reset procedure*)



Should you determine that the issue is not with the source device, the next step is a reset. Please proceed to Reset Instructions.







If the issue is constant, regardless of volume






Try connecting a different source device to the headphones to determine if the problem is with the device or headphones.




*If the Headphones model can’t be reset, please remove this reset procedure*)

Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




There are 3 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Broken jack on the source device

  • Broken wire

  • Broken connector on the headphones


First, let’s determine if the source device (Phone, iPad, Computer, etc.) is giving the problem. Please try connecting to a different source using the same wire and headphones. If the problem is resolved, this means that the jack in your phone is no longer working properly.




If the problem is not resolved, switch back to the original device and try the following to see if any of these things change the number of dropouts.


  1. Flex the wire where it joins with the source device. If there is a change in dropouts, this means that the wire is bad. Proceed to Next Steps.

  2. Flex the wire where it joins with the headphones.


    • Detachable wire: If there is a change in dropouts, this means that either the wire is bad or the jack in the headphones is failing. Proceed to step 3.

    • Non-Detachable wire: If there is a change in dropouts, proceed to Next Steps.



  3. By making subtle movements, see if you can determine whether the wire or headphone jack is the problem. Should you determine that the wire is the problem, a new wire is necessary. On the other hand, if the headphone jack is the issue, the headphone needs servicing. Proceed to Next Steps.

Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




There are 4 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Dust/Dirt/Debris blocking the ear tip screen

  • Balance Control in your source device or music player app

  • Source Device

  • Damaged Wire



Cleaning The Eartips


This is the most common reason for no sound/lack of sound issues. A simple cleaning will almost always fix this problem. Please click on this link for detailed online instructions.




You may also check out these videos for best practices on how to keep your True Wireless (TWS) headphones and In-Ear headphones at their best sound performance.



Checking Balance Control


If cleaning doesn't solve the problem, the next thing to check is the balance control. This allows you to make one side louder than the other. Be sure that the left/right balance control is set to default (centered).



  1. Check the balance control on your source device by going to the "Accessibility" settings.

  2. Check the balance control on your music player app, commonly found in the playback or EQ settings.



Different Source Device


If this doesn't solve the issue, we need to determine if the problem is in the device or the headphones. Try to connect the headphones to a different device (phone/tablet/music player) to see if it fixes the problem.



Damaged Wire



  1. Flex the wire where it joins with the source device. If any sound is heard, this means that the wire is bad. Proceed to Next Steps.

    • Non-Detachable wire: If any sound is heard, proceed to Next Steps.

Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




There are 5 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Line of sight

  • Electrical Interference

  • Wireless Interference

  • Corrupt Bluetooth connection

  • Source device issues


First, Bluetooth, in a perfect environment, will perform well for up to 30 feet. However, walls, obstacles, and other wireless devices can impede that 30-foot range. If it works well at 10 feet or less, it is likely that there is something interfering with your wireless Bluetooth signal, causing these dropouts.

queryResult.htmlBody:
Hello {!Contact.FirstName},




Thank you for contacting Harman Customer Support.




There are 3 potential causes for a problem like this.


  • Volume level on the source device is too loud

  • Volume level on the speaker is too loud

  • Source Device


If the volume changes (aka pumping) only occurs as the volume is increased to loud levels, this means the unit is working by design. As the internal amplifier reaches its limits, an internal limiter engages in order to protect itself from damage. There is no way to bypass this.




If the speaker cannot play loud enough to your liking, you may want to consider a bigger, more powerful speaker.




On the other hand, if the volume changes (aka pumping) occurs at all volume levels, the volume on the source device may be too loud. Try turning the volume down on the device to see if it fixes the issue. If this does not fix the problem, please try connecting the speaker to a different device (phone/tablet/music player) to see if the problem is in the device or the speaker.




If the problem still occurs with a different device, please try a reset. Reset may fix the issue, much in the way rebooting a computer or phone fixes many problems.




Note: RESET will wipe all previous settings and pairings, so it will be necessary to pair your unit with your devices again.
